headline: Failed House rule would have set up debate on a defense spending bill and three bills about digital currencies and stablecoins.
what_it_does: This was a procedural resolution that would have set the terms for House debate and votes on four bills. These were a Defense Department spending bill for the 2026 budget year (H.R. 4016), a bill on how the SEC and CFTC regulate the sale of digital commodities (H.R. 3633), a bill to bar the Federal Reserve from offering certain products or services directly to individuals and from using a central bank digital currency (H.R. 1919), and a Senate bill to regulate payment stablecoins (S. 1582). It would also have waived a House rule so that certain resolutions from the Rules Committee could be taken up more quickly. The resolution itself would not have changed any law; it only controlled how the House would consider these bills.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the House of Representatives
who_it_affects.how: They would have debated and voted on the four bills under the time limits and procedures set by this resolution.
